name: Prompt and Model Versioning
question: What exactly was running when it broke?
summary: Treat the prompt, the model snapshot, the tool set and the parameters as one versioned release. Pin dated model snapshots instead of aliases the provider can move, keep prompts in a registry with labels such as production and staging, and stamp every trace with the release. Then rollback is a label move, and every trace says exactly what ran.
useCases: More than one person changes prompts, or prompts change weekly
You depend on a hosted model that is updated or retired on the provider’s schedule
Audits or incidents need to know which prompt produced an answer

items.detail: an alias such as claude-sonnet-4-5 can move; a dated snapshot such as claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 does not
numbered versions with labels; code loads by label, not by pasted text
prompt + model + tools + parameters, hashed into one id
the release id on every root span
move the production label back one version; no redeploy
providers deprecate snapshots on a published schedule, so plan migrations

steps: Move prompts out of code into a registry and load them by label
Pin a dated model snapshot in the release configuration
Stamp every trace with the release id
Roll back by moving the label; upgrade snapshots through a canary
pitfalls: An alias in the config lets the provider change your model without a deploy
Prompts edited in a dashboard with no review or eval gate

comparison.scope: What changed, and how to undo it

code.text: template="Summarise the claim. Cite the clause.\n\n{{claim}}",

steps.title: Register a version
steps.text: Each change becomes a numbered version with a commit message. The model configuration travels with the prompt, so a version means prompt text and model settings together.

steps.title: Promote only after evals
steps.text: The production alias moves to the new version only when the offline suite passes. Nobody edits the live text directly.

steps.title: Load by alias
steps.text: Application code asks for claims-review@production. It never contains the prompt text, so promotion needs no redeploy.

steps.title: Stamp the trace
steps.text: Every span records the prompt version and the model. When an answer is questioned, the trace says exactly which release produced it.

steps.title: Pin a snapshot, not an alias
steps.text: claude-sonnet-4-5 is an alias the provider can move; claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 is a fixed snapshot. Pinning means the model only changes when you change it.

steps.title: Roll back with one call
steps.text: If v13 misbehaves, point production back at v12. The next request loads v12; nothing is rebuilt or redeployed.

library.name: MLflow Prompt Registry
library.what: Versioned prompts with aliases such as production, commit messages and an attached model configuration, loaded by URI.

practice.note: Record the prompt name, version and model snapshot on every trace so an incident can be tied to one release.

samples.code:
import mlflow

# Register a new version (the template uses {{double braces}})
p = mlflow.genai.register_prompt(
    name="claims-review",
    template="Summarise this claim for the desk. Cite the policy clause.\n\n{{claim}}",
    commit_message="Add clause citation",
    model_config={"model_name": "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",   # a pinned snapshot
                  "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 800},
)

# Promote it after offline evals pass
mlflow.genai.set_prompt_alias(name="claims-review", alias="production", version=p.version)

# Application code loads by alias, never by pasted text
prompt = mlflow.genai.load_prompt("prompts:/claims-review@production")
text = prompt.format(claim="Hospitalisation, 3 days, cashless request ...")
model = prompt.model_config["model_name"]

# Rollback: point the alias at the previous version; no redeploy
mlflow.genai.set_prompt_alias(name="claims-review", alias="production", version=p.version - 1)

numericDrill.question: A config uses a model alias. Overnight the provider starts serving a new snapshot to 80% of your traffic. The old snapshot succeeds on 94% of tasks and the new one on 84%. What is your overall success rate now, in percent?
numericDrill.answer: 0.8 × 84 + 0.2 × 94 = 67.2 + 18.8 = 86.0%. An 8-point drop with no deploy on your side; pinning the old snapshot restores 94%.

interview.question: What belongs in a versioned agent release?
interview.answer: Everything that changes behaviour: the prompt text and version, the model snapshot, the tool definitions and their versions, and generation parameters such as temperature and max tokens. Hash them into one release id and stamp it on every trace, so any answer can be traced to exactly what produced it.

interview.question: Why not always use the model alias to get improvements automatically?
interview.answer: Because the change arrives untested, on the provider’s schedule, and can shift behaviour your prompts depend on. Pin a dated snapshot, and move to a new one deliberately: run offline evals, then a canary, then promote. Also track the snapshot’s retirement date so the migration is planned.

mistakes.mistake: Editing the live prompt in a dashboard without review
mistakes.fix: Promote a new version by moving a label only after evals pass

mistakes.mistake: Calling a moving alias in production
mistakes.fix: Pin a dated snapshot and upgrade through a canary

quiz.question: A portfolio assistant’s config says model: claude-sonnet-4-5. Why is this risky in production?
options: It is an alias, which the provider can point at a new snapshot without your deploy
It is a deprecated model
It disables prompt caching
It limits the context window
quiz.explanation: An alias can move; a dated snapshot such as claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 stays fixed until you change it.

quiz.question: A bank’s letter-drafting prompt lives as a string in the code. A bad edit ships. What is the main cost of this setup during rollback?
options: The model must be retrained
A code change and redeploy are needed to undo it
Traces are deleted
The registry label cannot move
quiz.explanation: With prompts in code, rollback is a deploy; with a registry, it is a label move.

quiz.question: Which set of items should one versioned agent release bundle?
options: Only the prompt text
The prompt and the user’s question
Prompt version, model snapshot, tool definitions and generation parameters
The trace backend and the dashboard
quiz.explanation: Anything that changes behaviour belongs in the release, so an answer can be tied to exactly what produced it.

quiz.question: A provider starts serving a new snapshot behind your alias to 60% of traffic. The old snapshot succeeds 95% of the time and the new one 85%. What is your overall success rate?
A SaaS team moves prompts to a registry. Which practices make that worthwhile? Select all that apply.
options: Load prompts in code by label, such as production
Promote a new version only after evals pass
Let anyone edit the live production text directly
Copy the prompt text into each service for speed
quiz.explanation: Loading by label and gated promotion give fast, safe rollout; direct edits and copies bypass the registry.

quiz.question: A team pins a dated snapshot. What ongoing work does that create?
options: None; pinned snapshots are supported forever
Tracking the snapshot’s retirement date and planning upgrades
Re-registering the prompt every day
Disabling traces
quiz.explanation: Providers retire snapshots on a schedule, so pinned releases need planned migrations.

quiz.question: An auditor asks which prompt produced a customer letter sent three weeks ago. What makes this answerable in seconds?
options: Keeping the letter in email
The model’s own memory
The release id, including the prompt version, stamped on the trace for that request
Asking the engineer who wrote the prompt
quiz.explanation: A release stamp on each trace ties every output to the exact prompt and model version.

quiz.question: In MLflow’s prompt registry, how does application code usually load the live prompt?
options: By the alias URI, such as prompts:/claims-review@production
By pasting the latest text into the code
By version number hard-coded in every service
By downloading it from the trace backend
quiz.explanation: Loading by alias lets promotion and rollback happen by moving the alias.

quiz.question: A clinical-summary team needs to roll back a bad prompt quickly and prove what ran. Which do they need? Select all that apply.
options: A registry with numbered versions and a production label
The prompt version recorded on every trace
A larger model
More examples in the prompt
quiz.explanation: Versions plus labels give fast rollback; trace stamps give proof. Model size and examples are unrelated.

quiz.question: Prompt v13 is live and misbehaving. Using a registry with aliases, what is the fastest safe rollback?
options: Delete version 13
Point the production alias back at version 12
Edit version 13’s text in place
Restart the service
quiz.explanation: Moving the alias restores v12 on the next request and keeps v13 for investigation.

quiz.question: Why store the model configuration, such as snapshot and temperature, with the prompt version?
options: Prompts only work with one temperature
It makes the prompt shorter
The provider requires it
A prompt tuned for one model and setting can behave differently on another, so they change together
quiz.explanation: Prompt and model settings interact, so versioning them together keeps a release reproducible.

quiz.question: A bank’s agent broke after the provider changed the model behind its alias. Which measures would have prevented or shortened this? Select all that apply.
options: Pinning a dated snapshot
Recording the served model on traces
Adding a longer system prompt
Raising the temperature
quiz.explanation: Pinning prevents the silent change; recording the served model makes it visible at once.

quiz.question: An EdTech company changes its tutoring prompt weekly. Which statement about using Git alone for prompts is correct?
options: It gives review and history, but rollback still needs a deploy
It cannot store text files
It rolls back instantly without a deploy
It records which snapshot served each request
quiz.explanation: Git gives history and review; runtime label moves need a registry or config service.

quiz.question: A team upgrades to a new model snapshot. What is the right order?
options: Switch production, then run evals
Run offline evals, canary the new snapshot, then promote
Change the alias and wait for complaints
Upgrade only the prompt
quiz.explanation: Offline evals catch known problems, the canary catches live ones, and only then does everyone get it.

quiz.question: Which of these change an agent’s behaviour and should therefore be part of its versioned release? Select all that apply.
options: The tool definitions and their descriptions
The generation temperature
The on-call rota
The colour of the admin dashboard
quiz.explanation: Tool descriptions and parameters change what the model does; rotas and dashboards do not.

quiz.question: A release record is hashed into one id, cfg-7f3a. What is the main benefit?
options: It compresses the prompt
It encrypts the release
It speeds up the model
One short id on every trace identifies the whole configuration that ran
quiz.explanation: A single id makes filtering traces and comparing releases simple.

quiz.question: Three teams edit the same support prompt in a shared dashboard, and a bad edit went live on a Friday. What is the best process fix?
options: Lock the dashboard permanently
Let only one engineer edit prompts
Any edit creates a version; promotion to production needs review and passing evals
Stop changing the prompt
quiz.explanation: Versioned drafts keep teams fast, while gated promotion keeps production safe.

quiz.question: A fintech wants every answer traceable to what produced it. Which three things together make that true? Select all that apply.
options: Prompts from a registry version
A pinned model snapshot
The release stamped on every trace
A bigger context window
quiz.explanation: All three are needed: the prompt version, a fixed model and the stamp that records them.

quiz.question: A pinned snapshot is announced for retirement in 60 days. What should the team do?
options: Nothing until it stops working
Evaluate the replacement offline, canary it, and promote before the date
Switch to the alias permanently
Remove the model from the release
quiz.explanation: Retirements are scheduled, so migrate deliberately through evals and a canary.

quiz.question: An incident timeline shows: 90 minutes to find which prompt was live, 45 minutes to redeploy. Which changes cut both? Select all that apply.
options: Stamping the prompt version on traces
Loading prompts from a registry by label
Doubling the on-call team
Writing longer prompts
quiz.explanation: The stamp removes the search; the registry replaces the redeploy with a label move.
